route: Employment Licence (Jobsplus) and residence permit for employment under six months; Single Permit for six months or more

permit.applies: The employer applies to Jobsplus for the employment licence; the third-country national then applies to Identità for the residence permit through the Expatriates Portal.
permit.first: An employment licence from Jobsplus for the engagement's period; for culture and entertainment no search for EEA, Swiss or Maltese candidates is needed, but the covering letter must give the reasons for choosing the third-country nationals.

permit.eligibility: Entertainers, musicians and crew members on film productions, for which the employer will need to elaborate in the covering letter on the reasons for the choice of the third country nationals concerned.

sources.title: Identità, Expatriates Unit: Non-EU Nationals – Employment Under Six Months
sources.said: A third-country national employed for less than six months may apply for a residence permit upon the presentation of a valid employment license issued for that period from Jobsplus. … Such permit is NOT renewable. In case the third-country national wishes to reside and work in Malta for six months or more, a Single Work Permit is required. An application with Identità for Employment Less than 6 Months can be submitted through the Expatriates Portal against a fee of €50.
